rows.pymc: PyMC Labs (company behind PyMC); community contributors; PyPI owner PyMC Labs.
rows.meridian: Google (Marketing/ads measurement team); open source under google GitHub org.
rows.robyn: Meta Marketing Science (facebookexperimental org); R maintainer Bernardo Lares; authors incl. Gufeng Zhou, Igor Skokan, Leonel Sentana.
rows.international_relevance: Vendor neutrality matters for multinational advertisers: Meridian and Robyn are built by the two largest ad platforms (potential perceived bias towards their channels); PyMC-Marketing is platform-independent. Discuss governance in class.

rows.pymc: First PyPI release 0.0.2 on 9 Feb 2023; 1.0.0 on 7 Aug 2026 ('Multidimensional MMM is now the MMM').
rows.meridian: Successor to Google's LightweightMMM. Changelog lists 0.x releases from mid-2024 (public preview), GA version 1.0.0 on 24 Jan 2025; 2.0.0 on 2 Sep 2026 (JAX default).
rows.robyn: R package open-sourced by Meta around 2021 (exact first date not verified here); v3.x line since then; Python port robynpy first released 8 May 2024.
rows.international_relevance: All three are young; teaching material older than 2025 may describe outdated APIs (e.g. PyMC-Marketing's old DelayedSaturatedMMM / MMM class removed in 1.0, Meridian's TensorFlow backend deprecated).

rows.meridian: 2.1.0 (PyPI 25 Sep 2026; changelog entry dated 17 Sep 2026).
rows.robyn: CRAN 3.12.1 (2 Jul 2025); GitHub tag v3.12.0 marked latest; robynpy 0.3.6 (3 Apr 2025, beta). Release cadence has slowed markedly since mid-2025.
rows.international_relevance: Version pinning is essential for reproducible student labs across semesters.

rows.pymc: Apache-2.0.
rows.meridian: Apache-2.0 (GitHub repo licence).
rows.robyn: MIT.
rows.international_relevance: All permissive, commercial use allowed; no licence barrier for subsidiaries in different countries.

rows.pymc: Python (>= 3.12).
rows.meridian: Python (3.11-3.13 per install docs).
rows.robyn: R (>= 4.0.0); Python beta port 'robynpy' (rewrite of R 3.11.1, Python >= 3.8) and an R-plumber based Python API (beta).
rows.international_relevance: Course choice R vs Python determines which tool students can run; WU marketing programmes often teach R.

rows.pymc: PyMC 6 / PyTensor 3 / ArviZ 1.2; samplers: PyMC NUTS, NumPyro, BlackJAX, Nutpie.
rows.meridian: JAX default since 2.0.0 (float64 default; MERIDIAN_ENABLE_JAX_X64 to switch); TensorFlow Probability backend deprecated; NUTS MCMC.
rows.robyn: glmnet (ridge regression) + Nevergrad (Python, via reticulate) for hyperparameter search + prophet for decomposition + nloptr for the budget allocator.
rows.international_relevance: Bayesian backends (PyMC, JAX) scale to many countries x channels via hierarchical models; Robyn fits each market separately so compute grows linearly with markets.

rows.pymc: pip install pymc-marketing (or conda/mamba conda-forge recommended for compiled PyMC dependencies).
rows.meridian: pip install google-meridian; extras: [and-cuda] (GPU), [colab], [mlflow], [jax], [schema], [scenarioplanner], [geox].
rows.robyn: install.packages('Robyn') from CRAN, plus Python Nevergrad via reticulate (reticulate::py_install('nevergrad')); or pip install robynpy.
rows.international_relevance: Robyn's mixed R+Python dependency is the most common installation failure in student labs; budget a setup session or use cloud notebooks.

rows.pymc: CPU fine for small models; GPU acceleration through JAX-based samplers (NumPyro/BlackJAX).
rows.meridian: GPU recommended for geo models ([and-cuda] extra; Colab GPU notebooks provided); CPU possible for national models.
rows.robyn: CPU only; parallel cores via doParallel (cores argument). No GPU.
rows.international_relevance: Hierarchical models with 10-30 countries x 100+ weeks can take long on laptops; Colab GPUs help for Meridian.

rows.pymc: Fully Bayesian (priors on all parameters, posterior distributions).
rows.meridian: Fully Bayesian hierarchical (geo-level) model.
rows.robyn: Frequentist ridge regression (L2-penalised OLS) with hyperparameters (adstock, saturation, lambda, train size) tuned by multi-objective evolutionary search; not Bayesian.
rows.international_relevance: Bayesian priors offer a principled way to transfer knowledge from large to small countries; Robyn has no formal mechanism for cross-market borrowing.

rows.pymc: MCMC (NUTS) by default; variational/other samplers via PyMC options.
rows.meridian: MCMC NUTS (sample_posterior), prior sampling (sample_prior).
rows.robyn: Nevergrad TwoPointsDE (default algorithm) proposes hyperparameters; glmnet fits ridge for each candidate; iterations x trials (demo: 2000 iterations, 5 trials).
rows.international_relevance: MCMC diagnostics (R-hat, divergences) need teaching time; Robyn runtime driven by iterations x trials x markets.

rows.pymc: Single posterior; model comparison via LOO/WAIC (ArviZ), posterior predictive checks; no Pareto front.
rows.meridian: Single posterior; model quality checks (Model Health Summary Card, ModelReviewer, R-hat, prior-posterior shift); AKS uses AIC for knots.
rows.robyn: Multi-objective: NRMSE (fit), DECOMP.RSSD (distance between spend share and effect share), MAPE.LIFT (calibration error); Pareto-optimal models, then k-means clustering to shortlist; analyst picks a final model (objective_weights since 3.10.5).
rows.international_relevance: Robyn's DECOMP.RSSD encodes a business-plausibility prior (effects near spend shares) that may not hold across markets with different media maturity; analyst choice among Pareto models adds subjectivity per country.

rows.pymc: Explicit: dag, treatment_nodes, outcome_node arguments for causal identification from a DAG; pm.do interventions.
rows.meridian: Documented distinction of confounders (controls) vs treatments (paid/organic media, non-media treatments); no DAG API.
rows.robyn: No explicit causal API; relies on calibration with experiments for causal grounding.
rows.international_relevance: Confounders differ by country (e.g. macro shocks, competitor entry); DAG thinking helps decide which controls to include per market.

rows.pymc: GeometricAdstock, DelayedAdstock, WeibullCDFAdstock, WeibullPDFAdstock, BinomialAdstock, NoAdstock (half-life parameterisation available since 1.1.0); l_max lag window.
rows.meridian: Weighted lag with max_lag; adstock_decay_spec: geometric (default) or binomial (since 1.2.0), per-channel decay possible.
rows.robyn: adstock = 'geometric' (theta), 'weibull_cdf' or 'weibull_pdf' (shape, scale; allows delayed peak).
rows.international_relevance: Carryover can differ by country (e.g. TV culture, media inflation); allow country-specific or partially pooled decay.

rows.pymc: LogisticSaturation, HillSaturation, HillSaturationSigmoid, MichaelisMentenSaturation, TanhSaturation, TanhSaturationBaselined, LogSaturation, RootSaturation, InverseScaledLogisticSaturation, NoSaturation.
rows.meridian: Hill(ec, slope) only.
rows.robyn: Hill (alpha = shape, gamma = inflection).
rows.international_relevance: Saturation points depend on market size: population scaling (Meridian) or per-geo scaling (PyMC-Marketing) makes curves comparable across countries.

rows.pymc: adstock_first=True default (adstock then saturation); configurable.
rows.meridian: hill_before_adstock=False default (adstock then Hill); configurable. For R&F: Hill on frequency, times reach, then adstock.
rows.robyn: Adstock then saturation (fixed).
rows.international_relevance: Order changes response-curve interpretation; keep identical across countries for comparability.

rows.pymc: yearly_seasonality (Fourier modes), events module, intercept, optional linear trend components; controls.
rows.meridian: Time-varying intercept via knots (piecewise-linear interpolation; knots argument; automatic knot selection enable_aks); no built-in Fourier seasonality (seasonality via knots or controls).
rows.robyn: Prophet decomposition (prophet_vars: trend, season, monthly, weekday, holiday) added as regressors.
rows.international_relevance: Seasonality differs across hemispheres and cultures (e.g. Ramadan, Singles' Day, Christmas); per-country seasonal terms are needed.

rows.pymc: time_varying_intercept and time_varying_media accept bool or HSGP config (Hilbert-space Gaussian process); HSGP composable as terms (1.3.0).
rows.meridian: Time-varying intercept only (knots); media coefficients constant over time (not documented as time-varying).
rows.robyn: Not supported (coefficients static within the window; refresh re-estimates).
rows.international_relevance: Media effectiveness drifts differently in markets after shocks (e.g. COVID, inflation); TV-coefficient models capture this.

rows.pymc: events module (event transformations, user-supplied event calendars); no bundled country holiday table.
rows.meridian: Not bundled; holidays as control variables or via time knots.
rows.robyn: Bundled dt_prophet_holidays (demo.R: '123 countries included'); select one country via prophet_country; custom holidays can be added.
rows.international_relevance: Robyn makes country holiday effects easy (e.g. prophet_country='AT'); only one country per model, so multi-country panels need separate models.

rows.pymc: National or panel: dims=('geo',) (or brand, product, country) since 1.0 multidimensional MMM; data must be rectangular across dims.
rows.meridian: Geo-level recommended; national model = single-geo special case.
rows.robyn: National (one time series per model); geo/market modelling = separate models per market.
rows.international_relevance: Country = natural 'geo' in international marketing; panels across EU markets make the hierarchical tools attractive.

rows.pymc: Flexible per-parameter: complete pooling (no geo dim), no pooling (dims incl. geo), or partial pooling (Prior with dims=('channel','geo'), centered=False, hyperpriors shared over geo).
rows.meridian: Built-in hierarchy: geo media coefficients drawn around a national mean (media_effects_dist LOG_NORMAL or NORMAL) with spread eta_m; controls with xi_c; geo baselines tau_g; adstock/Hill shared across geos.
rows.robyn: Not supported.
rows.international_relevance: Partial pooling lets small markets (e.g. Austria, Slovenia) borrow strength from large ones (Germany) while keeping country-specific effects.

rows.pymc: scaling argument (default max-abs scaling of target and channels; per-geo scaling with dims=()); population not a required input.
rows.meridian: Population per geo is a required input; KPI and media are population-scaled (per-capita) internally; control_population_scaling_id for controls; ModelSpec population-scaling vocabulary in 2.1.0.
rows.robyn: No population scaling (single series).
rows.international_relevance: Per-capita scaling puts small and large countries on a comparable scale; for countries also consider purchasing power.

rows.pymc: One pooled model across countries, or separate models with priors informed by a reference market.
rows.meridian: One geo model per country (regions within a country) or countries as geos (if KPI/media comparable); docs guidance for US DMAs (top 50-100 by population).
rows.robyn: One model per market; repeat pipeline; compare via one-pagers.
rows.international_relevance: Choice of 'countries as geos' requires common currency and comparable KPI definitions.

rows.pymc: All priors configurable via model_config / Prior objects (pymc_extras), including dims-aware hierarchical priors.
rows.meridian: PriorDistribution object; treatment prior types via media_prior_type / *_prior_type: 'roi', 'mroi', 'contribution', 'coefficient' (since 1.1.0).
rows.robyn: No priors; hyperparameter bounds (e.g. theta ranges: TV 0.3-0.8, OOH/print/radio 0.1-0.4, digital 0-0.3) act as constraints.
rows.international_relevance: Priors are the vehicle for cross-country knowledge transfer; bounds in Robyn can be set per market.

rows.pymc: ROAS calibration via add_cost_per_target_calibration (1.0.0; link-aware for log link in 1.3.0); direct ROI reparameterisation not default.
rows.meridian: Core feature: ROI prior per channel (roi_m, roi_rf; LogNormal default type; helpers lognormal_dist_from_mean_std, lognormal_dist_from_range); mROI priors; roi_calibration_period to restrict window.
rows.robyn: Not supported (no priors).
rows.international_relevance: ROI priors in local currency must be converted consistently if countries are pooled.

rows.pymc: add_lift_test_measurements(df) with columns channel, x, delta_x, delta_y, sigma (+ dims such as geo): tests treated as noisy observations of the saturation curve (signed Normal likelihood in 1.3.0).
rows.meridian: Experiments translated into ROI priors; CalibrationBuilder adjusts for recency, duration, spend, granularity; GeoX results via with_meridian_geox_experiment_result (2.0.0, [geox] extra).
rows.robyn: calibration_input data frame (channel, liftStartDate, liftEndDate, liftAbs, spend, confidence, metric, calibration_scope); MAPE.LIFT added as third objective.
rows.international_relevance: Experiments are often run only in large markets; calibrated hierarchical models can propagate that information to untested countries (PyMC-Marketing/Meridian), Robyn only calibrates the market where the test ran.

rows.pymc: Channel columns in any unit; cost_per_unit argument to map to spend for ROAS/optimisation; PowerPriceResponse for spend-dependent costs (1.3.0).
rows.meridian: media (impressions etc.) plus media_spend required for ROI; spend preferred when unit is not spend.
rows.robyn: paid_media_spends plus optional paid_media_vars (exposure); since 3.12.0 exposure fitting prioritised over spend.
rows.international_relevance: Media prices (CPMs) vary strongly by country; modelling exposure and converting with local CPM avoids conflating price and effectiveness.

rows.pymc: Not natively supported (can enter as custom regressors / MuEffects).
rows.meridian: Native: reach and frequency inputs for paid and organic channels; effect = reach x Hill(frequency), adstocked; optimal_freq() for frequency recommendations.
rows.robyn: Curve calibrator (robyn_calibrate, beta) using R&F data; R&F allocator prototype, not production.
rows.international_relevance: R&F data availability differs by country and platform (e.g. YouTube/Meta yes, local TV panels vary).

rows.pymc: control_columns (not auto-scaled), events, custom MuEffects (funnel/mediator effects).
rows.meridian: organic_media (adstock+Hill), organic R&F, non_media_treatments (linear, no transform), controls (confounders).
rows.robyn: organic_vars (adstock+saturation), context_vars (controls), factor_vars.
rows.international_relevance: Price, promotions, distribution and macro controls must be harmonised (definitions, units) across countries.

rows.pymc: Channel contributions, ROAS / cost per target, response curves, decomposition (get_contributions, period aggregation since 1.2.0).
rows.meridian: ROI, mROI, CPIK (cost per incremental KPI), incremental outcome, effectiveness, response curves, optimal frequency; HTML summary report; Model Health card.
rows.robyn: ROAS or CPA, mROAS, response curves (robyn_response), waterfall decomposition, one-pager per model.
rows.international_relevance: CPIK/CPA in local currency enables comparisons when KPIs are non-revenue (e.g. app installs in multiple countries).

rows.pymc: Full posterior credible intervals for all quantities.
rows.meridian: Full posterior credible intervals for ROI/mROI/CPIK etc.
rows.robyn: Bootstrapped confidence intervals on ROAS within model clusters (robyn_clusters); point estimates per selected model.
rows.international_relevance: Small markets yield wide intervals; communicating them avoids over-allocation to noisy countries.

rows.pymc: BudgetOptimizerWrapper.optimize_budget / BudgetOptimizer.allocate_budget; scipy SLSQP; custom utility (default mean response; risk-aware notebook); custom Constraint objects; evaluate_plan.
rows.meridian: BudgetOptimizer.optimize; fixed_budget True (budget, pct_of_spend) or flexible (target_roi / target_mroi); grid-based search over spend; WeeklyOptimizationGrid (2.0.0).
rows.robyn: robyn_allocator scenarios 'max_response' and 'target_efficiency' (ROAS/CPA target); nloptr gradient-based optimisation; demo warns results 'require further validation'.
rows.international_relevance: Budget optimisation should account for posterior uncertainty especially in small markets.

rows.pymc: budget_bounds per channel x geo (lower/upper), budget_distribution_over_period over dates.
rows.meridian: spend_constraint_lower / spend_constraint_upper per channel (default 0.3 for fixed budget, i.e. keep >=70% of spend).
rows.robyn: channel_constr_low / channel_constr_up per paid channel (order of paid_media_selected).
rows.international_relevance: Country-level minimum spends (brand presence, contracts) must enter as constraints.

rows.pymc: Yes: decision variables over channel x geo in one optimisation (allocation across countries possible if countries are a dim).
rows.meridian: Channel-level allocation of a total budget; explicit geo-level allocation not documented.
rows.robyn: Not supported (per-market allocator; cross-market allocation must be done manually).
rows.international_relevance: Key differentiator for international budget setting (how much to Germany vs Austria vs CEE).

rows.pymc: Optimise for future windows with planned control values (1.3.0); what-if via sample_posterior_predictive on new data.
rows.meridian: Scenario Planner modules ([scenarioplanner] extra, 1.4.0) with interactive dashboards (Colab / Data Studio); optimisation with forecasted data.
rows.robyn: Allocator scenarios on historical windows; robyn_response for what-if spend.
rows.international_relevance: Scenario tools help country managers explore local plans with the HQ model.

rows.pymc: Out-of-sample prediction on new data; time-slice cross-validation notebooks (not re-verified for 1.3.0).
rows.meridian: holdout_id in ModelSpec for holdout fit; 2.1.0 declarative holdouts in ModelSpec.
rows.robyn: ts_validation: train/validation/test split with train size as hyperparameter; NRMSE on test.
rows.international_relevance: Hold out a country or period to test transferability of pooled estimates.

rows.pymc: sample_posterior_predictive, ArviZ diagnostics (R-hat, ESS, divergences), prior predictive checks.
rows.meridian: R-hat summary, prior vs posterior plots, EDAEngine / MeridianEDA (VIF, cost-per-unit checks), Bayesian PPP check, ModelReviewer.
rows.robyn: Fit plots, Pareto plots, convergence plots of Nevergrad, one-pagers; no PPC (not Bayesian).
rows.international_relevance: Data quality checks per country (missing channels, outliers) should precede pooling.

rows.pymc: Refit on new data; MLflow autolog and load_mmm for model registry (Zarr format 1.3.0).
rows.meridian: Refit; model serialization (serde, ModelSpec saved with model in 2.1.0); MLflow autologging.
rows.robyn: robyn_refresh() updates an exported model with new data (rule of thumb <= 50% new data; feature 'not yet thoroughly tested').
rows.international_relevance: Rolling refresh per country with consistent spec ensures comparability over time.

rows.pymc: ~1.3k stars, 431 forks; frequent releases (1.0.0 Aug, 1.1.0 Aug, 1.2.0 Sep, 1.3.0 Oct 2026).
rows.meridian: ~1.6k stars, 308 forks; frequent releases (2.0.0 Sep, 2.1.0 Sep 2026).
rows.robyn: ~1.5k stars, 437 forks, ~100 open issues; last CRAN release Jul 2025; repo labelled 'experimental'.
rows.international_relevance: Active maintenance matters for multi-year deployments across markets.

rows.pymc: Extensive example notebooks (multidimensional, lift test, budget allocation, case studies), API reference.
rows.meridian: developers.google.com/meridian: user guide, advanced modelling, Colab demos, API reference (many translated pages).
rows.robyn: Website with features page, demo.R walkthrough, one-pager outputs; arXiv paper (Runge et al. 2024).
rows.international_relevance: Translated Meridian docs (incl. German) ease use in DACH teams.

rows.pymc: PyMC Labs consulting; third-party agencies.
rows.meridian: Google Meridian partner network (Partners page in docs) and Google Ads account teams.
rows.robyn: Meta Marketing Science partners and agencies; community Facebook group.
rows.international_relevance: Local partner availability (e.g. Austrian/German agencies) affects adoption in smaller markets.

rows.pymc: No official minimum; Bayesian priors help with short series; pooling across dims increases effective data.
rows.meridian: Rough guidance: data points = geos x time; national 2 years weekly with 26 parameters is 'too low'; example 105 geos x 156 weeks; use fewer channels/knots or tighter hierarchical priors (HalfNormal(0.1) on eta_m, xi_c) when data are scarce.
rows.robyn: Rule-of-thumb in community: ~ 2-3 years weekly and observations/variables ratio ~10:1 (not re-verified in current docs).
rows.international_relevance: Small countries with few regions (Austria: 9 Bundeslaender) give limited geo variation; consider countries as geos in a pooled model.

rows.pymc: Minutes for small national models; longer for many geos (faster with Nutpie/NumPyro).
rows.meridian: Minutes on GPU, longer on CPU for geo models.
rows.robyn: Typically 10-60+ minutes per market depending on iterations x trials (not benchmarked here).
rows.international_relevance: Lab sessions should use small datasets or pre-fitted models.

rows.pymc: Steep: Python + Bayesian concepts + PyMC idioms; best for analytics-track students.
rows.meridian: Medium-steep: Python, Bayesian, but opinionated defaults and Colab demos; good guided-lab option.
rows.robyn: Moderate: R script workflow (demo.R) with automated outputs; but hyperparameters and Pareto choice need explanation.
rows.international_relevance: Mixed-background international cohorts benefit from Colab-based labs without local installs.

rows.pymc: Not built-in; user must convert spend/revenue to a common currency (and optionally PPP) before pooling.
rows.meridian: Currency support for reporting (1.3.0) and currency_code (2.0.0) — labels outputs; conversion across geos not documented (user pre-processing).
rows.robyn: Not built-in; each market model can stay in local currency.
rows.international_relevance: Pooling countries requires common currency; exchange-rate swings can create spurious spend variation; PPP-adjust for comparing efficiency.

rows.pymc: User-supplied events.
rows.meridian: User-supplied controls.
rows.robyn: Bundled holidays for 123 countries via prophet_country.
rows.international_relevance: Austria-specific holidays (e.g. 8 Dec, Pentecost Monday) differ from Germany; ignoring them biases media effects.

rows.dimension: Different channel mixes / missing data per country
rows.pymc: Rectangular data across dims required; channels absent in a country must be zero-filled (and priors interpreted carefully).
rows.meridian: Geo data must share channels; national-only channels can be imputed but reduce accuracy (Sun et al. 2017); zero spend allowed.
rows.robyn: Each market model can have its own channel set.
rows.international_relevance: Robyn's flexibility vs. hierarchical models' coherence: classic trade-off in international MMM.

rows.pymc: Aggregated time-series data only; no user-level data; runs on-premise.
rows.meridian: Aggregated data only; runs locally/Colab; no data sent to Google by the library (not explicitly documented).
rows.robyn: Aggregated data; motivated by privacy changes (Runge et al. 2024).
rows.international_relevance: MMM is privacy-durable under GDPR/ePrivacy and post-cookie; EU teams favour on-premise open source.

rows.pymc: Yes, flexible hierarchical priors over country dim.
rows.meridian: Yes, built-in geo hierarchy (countries as geos) or informative ROI priors from reference market.
rows.robyn: No; only manual hyperparameter bounds transfer.
rows.international_relevance: Central for sparse small markets.

rows.dimension: Sparse data in small markets (e.g. Austria)
rows.pymc: Partial pooling, informative priors, lift-test calibration mitigate.
rows.meridian: National model for AT feasible only with few channels/knots; better: pool AT as a geo with DACH countries.
rows.robyn: Separate AT model risks overfitting; reduce variables, tighten bounds, calibrate.
rows.international_relevance: Practical lab case: DACH panel with AT as small geo.
